name: Zhibai Dihuang pill (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Few data, pill always added to other drugs: mouth-ulcer review says no adverse effects seen; 84 girls on GnRHa: reactions similar. Herbs, minerals not listed. No harm report names it.
text: Studies: a 2023 meta-analysis of 7 randomized trials (669 participants) in recurrent mouth ulcers, in which the pill, taken by mouth, was added to Western medicine and compared with Western medicine alone, reports in its qualitative analysis that no adverse effects were observed; the authors note limited methodological quality and small samples, and the abstract does not say how adverse effects were recorded. In a retrospective study of 84 girls with precocious or rapidly progressive puberty, adverse reactions were compared between diet and a gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue (GnRHa) with or without the pill, and their incidence was similar in the two groups; the abstract does not name the reactions. An umbrella review of four systematic reviews or meta-analyses of randomized trials of botanical preparations in children with central precocious puberty, in which favourable signals were reported mainly for four groups of interventions, among them Zhibai Dihuang-based preparations (preparations based on the formula, which may differ from this pill), states that adverse events were incompletely defined and may have been under-reported, and that long-term safety in children was rarely assessed. The cited abstracts do not list the formula's herbs or say whether it contains mineral ingredients. PubMed searches found no report of liver injury, kidney injury or heavy-metal contamination naming this pill. No interaction data were found in the cited sources; in both studies the pill was given with other medicines, and neither abstract reports an interaction.
